title.en: Exact state restoration under inverse and repeated moves

summary: Verify that discrete puzzle state returns exactly under repeated moves, inverses and reversed sequences.
objective: Repeating a quarter turn four times, applying a move with its inverse, and reversing a sequence each restore the exact state.
applies_when: A puzzle has discrete legal moves with exact inverses.
Presentation interpolates a turn while the model stores exact values.
A viewer can interrupt an in-flight move or orbit the camera.
intent_signals: undo does not fully restore the cube
check that four turns return the start state
example_prompts: Check the exact state restoration of this cube after move sequences.

principles: Puzzle state is discrete: positions and orientations are exact integers, and an in-flight animation must never be rounded back into that state.
Every legal move has an exact inverse, and a move composed with its inverse is the identity on the whole state, including pieces the move does not touch.
Order matters when undoing: a sequence is undone by the reversed sequence of inverse moves, which is the check that catches inverses applied in the wrong order.
implementation: Represent state as integer slot positions plus discrete orientation values and compare states by exact equality rather than by geometric proximity.
For each legal move apply it four times and compare with the start state, then apply it once followed by its inverse and compare again.
Apply a mixed sequence of at least twelve moves, then the reversed sequence of inverses, and compare with the start state.
Interrupt an in-flight animation with another input and confirm the committed state equals one of the two exact endpoints.
observable_checks: Four quarter turns of any face restore the exact state and every move followed by its inverse restores it; unaffected pieces are identical rather than merely close.
The reversed inverse sequence restores the start state exactly; restoring positions but not orientations identifies orientation bookkeeping as the defect.
Interrupting an animation leaves a committed state equal to one of the two exact endpoints, and camera orbit changes no state or face identity.

known_limits: Checks move algebra and state exactness; it does not validate arbitrary scrambles as reachable states or provide a solver.
Authored verification guidance; no puzzle implementation was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: In this notation the face letters denote clockwise quarter turns of the named outer face, a prime denotes the counter-clockwise quarter turn, and a suffix of two denotes a half turn.
claims.scope: The outer-face move subset of the cited regulations, version dated April 2026; wide moves, slice moves and whole-puzzle rotations are outside it.
